## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppādanirodhavāra* ("Section on Arising and Cessation") is the third subdivision of the process section (*pavattivāra*, Ya 5.2) within the *Saccayamaka* (Ya 5) of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005]. Within this framework, the *pavattivāra* investigates the circumstances of an individual being reborn or passing away in various existential planes [Anderson 1999]. In the *Uppādanirodhavāra*, the four noble truths (*cattāri ariyasaccāni*) are interrogated using paired catechisms to determine how each truth arises, ceases, or both arises and ceases in relation to the other truths across the temporal divisions of the present, past, and future [Anderson 1999].
Scholars observe that the process sections across the *Yamaka*—comprising origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*)—embody an early stage of Buddhist process metaphysics, conceptualizing phenomena as dynamic processes rather than substantial things [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Furthermore, these analyses mark a critical milestone in the development of the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness, introducing the subdivision of a temporal moment (*khaṇa*) into distinct moments of origination (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and cessation (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. SuttaCentral notes one translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral].
No historical parallels in non-Pali canonical collections are identified by SuttaCentral. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse (7,536 matching passages across 32 Pali texts), demonstrating the highly formulaic structure of the *Yamaka* [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments are with its companion sections in the *Saccayamaka*—the *Uppādavāra* (Ya 5.2.1, with 2,447 matches) and *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2, with 2,310 matches)—as well as corresponding process sections in other chapters, including the *Indriyayamaka* (Ya 10.2.1), *Dhātuyamaka* (Ya 9.2.1–3), and *Saṅkhārayamaka* (Ya 6.2.1–3), and commentary texts such as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects automated textual affinities with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises, including Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā* and the *Triṃśikāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
